words.enDefinition: An invitation that anyone in the intended group can accept.

examples.en: It was an open invite, so students from both seminar groups could join us.
examples.zh: 这次是「开放邀请」，所以两个研讨班的学生都可以加入。

examples.en: We posted an open invite for a picnic on the lawn after Friday's classes.
examples.zh: 我们发了「开放邀请」，约大家星期五下课后去草坪野餐。

collocations: put out an open invite
an open invite to the picnic
extend an open invite

words.enDefinition: Restricted to people who have been personally invited.

examples.en: The screening was invite-only because our friends were borrowing a very small room for it.
examples.zh: 这次放映「仅限受邀者参加」，因为朋友们借用的房间很小。

examples.en: I checked whether the picnic was invite-only before telling my new roommate about it.
examples.zh: 我先问野餐是否「仅限受邀者参加」，才把消息告诉新室友。

collocations: an invite-only gathering
an invite-only event
keep a party invite-only

words.enDefinition: To tell the person inviting you whether you will attend.

examples.en: The message asked us to RSVP before Friday so they could reserve enough seats.
examples.zh: 消息请我们在星期五之前「回复是否出席」，这样他们能留够座位。

examples.en: I forgot to RSVP for the picnic even though I had already saved the date.
examples.zh: 虽然我已经把那天腾出来了，还是忘了为野餐「回复是否出席」。

collocations: RSVP by Friday
RSVP for a party
RSVP to an invite

words.enDefinition: A guest that an invited person is allowed to bring.

examples.en: I asked whether I could bring a plus-one because my sister was visiting that weekend.
examples.zh: 姐姐那个周末要来，我就问这次邀请能不能「多带一位同伴」。

examples.en: My roommate came as my plus-one when our classmates booked a few extra seats.
examples.zh: 同学们多订了几个座位，室友就作为我「多带的那位同伴」一起来了。

collocations: bring a plus-one
allow a plus-one
list someone's plus-one

words.enDefinition: To come to an event with an additional friend.

examples.en: The invitation said I could bring a friend to the picnic after our seminar.
examples.zh: 邀请上写着，研讨课结束后的野餐我可以「带一位朋友来」。

examples.en: I asked if I could bring a friend to the screening in Maya's building.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「带一位朋友来」参加玛雅那栋楼里的放映活动。

collocations: be allowed to bring a friend
ask if you can bring a friend
invite someone to bring a friend

words.enDefinition: To distribute invitations to the people you would like to attend.

examples.en: We waited to send out invitations until we knew the courtyard would be available.
examples.zh: 我们等确认庭院可以用之后，才「发出邀请」。

examples.en: I offered to send out invitations while my roommate asked how many chairs we could borrow.
examples.zh: 我主动提出「发出邀请」，室友则去问能借到多少把椅子。

collocations: send out invitations by text
send out invitations a week early
send out invitations for the picnic

words.enDefinition: A list of the people invited to a gathering or event.

examples.en: Maya checked the guest list before asking whether we needed another table for the evening.
examples.zh: 玛雅查看了「宾客名单」，再问晚上要不要多摆一张桌子。

examples.en: My roommate asked me to add his sister to the guest list for the picnic.
examples.zh: 室友请我把他妹妹加到野餐的「宾客名单」里。

collocations: check the guest list
add someone to the guest list
put together a guest list

words.enDefinition: To limit the number of people involved in a gathering.

examples.en: We decided to keep it small because there were only six seats in the lounge.
examples.zh: 休息室只有六个座位，我们决定「办个小规模聚会」。

examples.en: Can we keep it small this time and just invite the people from our seminar?
examples.zh: 这次咱们能不能「就小范围聚一下」，只邀请研讨课上的同学？

collocations: want to keep it small
try to keep it small
keep it small this time

words.enDefinition: A friendly response saying additional people are welcome to join.

examples.en: I said “The more the merrier” when my roommate asked about inviting our neighbors.
examples.zh: 室友问能不能约上邻居，我说「人越多越热闹」。

examples.en: The more the merrier was our motto for the afternoon picnic in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 「人越多越热闹」是我们下午在庭院野餐的口号。

collocations: say the more the merrier
reply the more the merrier
tell them the more the merrier

words.enDefinition: An event anyone can attend under the stated entry conditions.

examples.en: The film screening was a public event, so our neighbors asked if they could join us.
examples.zh: 那场电影放映是「面向公众的活动」，所以邻居问能不能和我们一起去。

examples.en: We chose a public event at the art center because our friends study elsewhere.
examples.zh: 朋友们在别的学校读书，我们就选了艺术中心一场「面向公众的活动」。

collocations: go to a public event
attend a public event
advertise a public event

words.enDefinition: A meeting or social event meant for a limited invited group.

examples.en: They planned a private gathering for the four classmates who had worked on the exhibition.
examples.zh: 他们为一起做展览的四位同学安排了一场「私人聚会」。

examples.en: The courtyard was booked for a private gathering when we went past it after class.
examples.zh: 我们下课经过庭院时，那里已被预订举办一场「私人聚会」。

collocations: a small private gathering
attend a private gathering
arrange a private gathering

words.enDefinition: A social evening organized around watching a film together.

examples.en: We planned a movie night in the residence lounge after our last exam was over.
examples.zh: 最后一场考试结束后，我们计划在宿舍休息室办个「电影之夜」。

examples.en: Our movie night started later because half the group was coming from a class across campus.
examples.zh: 有一半人要从校园另一边下课后赶来，所以我们的「电影之夜」开始得晚了一点。

collocations: have a movie night
plan a movie night
pick a film for movie night

words.enDefinition: A gathering where people watch an event or program together as it is shown.

examples.en: My friend invited me to a watch party for the final in the student lounge.
examples.zh: 朋友邀请我去学生休息室参加决赛的「集体观看活动」。

examples.en: We moved the watch party to another flat because its living room had more seats.
examples.zh: 另一套公寓客厅的座位更多，我们就把「集体观看活动」搬到了那里。

collocations: host a watch party
join a watch party
a watch party for the final

words.enDefinition: A late morning meal shared with others on a weekend.

examples.en: We met for weekend brunch near campus before working on our posters that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午做海报之前，我们先在校园附近一起吃了「周末早午餐」。

examples.en: I asked my old flatmate to join us for weekend brunch after her Saturday shift.
examples.zh: 我约以前的室友星期六下班后和我们一起吃「周末早午餐」。

collocations: meet for weekend brunch
invite someone to weekend brunch
plan a weekend brunch

words.enDefinition: An informal outdoor meal or get-together planned for a group.

examples.en: We arranged a group picnic by the lake after most people finished their final exams.
examples.zh: 大多数人考完期末后，我们在湖边安排了一次「集体野餐」。

examples.en: I brought an extra blanket to the group picnic because the benches were already taken.
examples.zh: 长椅已经有人了，所以我给「集体野餐」多带了一条毯子。

collocations: plan a group picnic
go on a group picnic
bring something to a group picnic

words.enDefinition: A social event that comes together without much planning in advance.

examples.en: Our coffee break turned into an impromptu gathering when two other classmates walked past.
examples.zh: 另外两位同学路过后，我们喝咖啡的休息时间变成了一次「临时聚会」。

examples.en: We had an impromptu gathering in the courtyard after the afternoon seminar was canceled.
examples.zh: 下午的研讨课取消后，我们在庭院里搞了场「临时聚会」。

collocations: have an impromptu gathering
an impromptu gathering after class
turn into an impromptu gathering

words.enDefinition: To keep a gathering relaxed and simple without making it elaborate.

examples.en: We wanted to keep it low-key after exams, so we just met for tea.
examples.zh: 考完试我们想「简单低调地聚一下」，就只约着喝了个茶。

examples.en: Let's keep it low-key this time and play some music in the common room.
examples.zh: 这次「简单低调地办」吧，在公共休息室放点音乐就好。

collocations: decide to keep it low-key
keep it low-key this time
want to keep it low-key

words.enDefinition: To visit or join someone informally to have coffee together.

examples.en: Do you want to come for coffee after you finish your shift at the library?
examples.zh: 你在图书馆下班后，要不要「来喝杯咖啡」？

examples.en: Mina asked us to come for coffee when our morning lecture finished earlier than expected.
examples.zh: 上午的讲座提前结束，米娜请我们「来喝杯咖啡」。

collocations: invite someone to come for coffee
come for coffee after class
ask someone to come for coffee

words.enDefinition: An informal opener asking if anyone wants to join a proposed activity.

examples.en: I wrote “Anyone up for a picnic?” after seeing the forecast for Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 看到星期六下午的天气预报后，我发消息问「有人想一起野餐吗」？

examples.en: Leo asked “Anyone up for coffee after class?” while we were putting away our notebooks.
examples.zh: 我们收笔记本时，利奥问「下课后有人想一起喝咖啡吗」？

collocations: anyone up for a picnic
anyone up for coffee
anyone up for a short walk

words.enDefinition: An informal invitation to take part in an activity with the speaker's group.

examples.en: We are getting coffee after the workshop, so do you want to join us?
examples.zh: 研讨活动结束后我们要去喝咖啡，你「想加入我们吗」？

examples.en: We have an extra ticket for the screening tonight if you want to join us.
examples.zh: 我们今晚的放映活动多了一张票，你「想加入我们」的话可以一起来。

collocations: want to join us for coffee
want to join us after class
want to join us on Saturday

words.enDefinition: An informal condition used when inviting someone who may be nearby and available.

examples.en: We are getting coffee near the library after class if you're around this afternoon.
examples.zh: 下课后我们要去图书馆附近喝咖啡，「如果你下午在附近有空」可以一起来。

examples.en: You can still join us for a walk by the river if you're around after class.
examples.zh: 「如果你下课后在附近有空」，还可以和我们一起去河边走走。

collocations: come by if you're around
join us if you're around
stop for coffee if you're around

words.enDefinition: A casual question about someone's plans before suggesting a weekend activity.

examples.en: I asked “Any plans for the weekend?” before suggesting a picnic by the river.
examples.zh: 我先问了「周末有什么安排吗」，然后才提议去河边野餐。

examples.en: Do you have any plans for the weekend now that your last exam is over?
examples.zh: 你最后一门考试已经考完了，「周末有什么安排吗」？

collocations: ask about any plans for the weekend
have any plans for the weekend
check if someone has any plans for the weekend

words.enDefinition: An informal question asking whether additional people will attend an activity.

examples.en: Do you know if anyone else is coming before I ask for a larger table?
examples.zh: 我去要更大的桌子前，你知道「还有谁会来」吗？

examples.en: Maya asked “Anyone else coming?” while she was trying to count how many seats we needed.
examples.zh: 玛雅在算需要几个座位时问「还有谁会来」？

collocations: know if anyone else is coming
is anyone else coming to the picnic
ask if anyone else is coming

words.enDefinition: To find out whether people are interested in a proposed social activity.

examples.en: I'll put the picnic idea in our class chat to see if anyone's interested.
examples.zh: 我会把野餐的想法发到班级群里，「问问有没有人想参加」。

examples.en: We wanted to see if anyone's interested before booking a larger room for the film.
examples.zh: 我们打算先「问问有没有人想参加」，再订一间更大的房间看电影。

collocations: ask in the chat to see if anyone's interested
see if anyone's interested in the picnic
check first to see if anyone's interested

words.enDefinition: To agree on what people will do together and when.

examples.en: Can we make a plan now so I know whether to bring my camera tomorrow?
examples.zh: 我们能现在就「商量好安排」吗？这样我就知道明天要不要带相机了。

examples.en: We could make a plan after class once everyone knows when their last exams end.
examples.zh: 等大家都知道各自最后一场考试几点结束，我们可以下课后「商量好安排」。

collocations: make a plan for Saturday
make a plan in the chat
make a plan to meet after class

words.enDefinition: To agree on the calendar date when an event will take place.

examples.en: We wanted to set a date for the picnic before people booked their trains home.
examples.zh: 我们想在大家订好回家的火车票之前，把野餐的「日期定下来」。

examples.en: Could we set a date after our last exam so more people can come along?
examples.zh: 我们能不能把「日期定在」最后一场考试之后，好让更多人来？

collocations: set a date for the picnic
set a date that works for everyone
help set a date

words.enDefinition: To keep a particular date free for an event that will happen later.

examples.en: Can you save the date for the picnic even if we haven't chosen a park yet?
examples.zh: 虽然我们还没选好公园，你能先「预留这个日期」参加野餐吗？

examples.en: Maya asked us to save the date before she shared the rest of the details.
examples.zh: 玛雅先请我们「预留这个日期」，之后才发其他细节。

collocations: ask friends to save the date
send a save the date message
save the date for a picnic

words.enDefinition: A poll sent to a group to find out what its members prefer.

examples.en: I made a group poll so everyone could vote on which evening worked for them.
examples.zh: 我发起了「群内投票」，让大家选自己方便的晚上。

examples.en: The group poll ended in a tie between Friday evening and Saturday afternoon this week.
examples.zh: 本周星期五晚上和星期六下午在「群内投票」中得票相同。

collocations: send a group poll
answer the group poll
set up a group poll

words.expression: get a rough idea of numbers
words.lemma: get a rough idea of numbers
words.enDefinition: To find out approximately how many people are likely to come to an event.
acceptedEnVariants: get a rough idea of numbers

examples.en: We need to get a rough idea of numbers before choosing which courtyard to use.
examples.zh: 选在哪个庭院之前，我们得先「估一下人数」。

examples.en: I started a poll to get a rough idea of numbers for Friday's drawing session.
examples.zh: 我发起了投票，为星期五的绘画活动「估一下人数」。

collocations: try to get a rough idea of numbers
get a rough idea of numbers for the picnic
ask around to get a rough idea of numbers

words.enDefinition: An arrangement that has been suggested but is still subject to change.

examples.en: We have a tentative plan for Saturday, but two people still need to check their shifts.
examples.zh: 我们星期六有个「暂定安排」，不过还有两个人要看排班。

examples.en: I shared a tentative plan before anyone spent money on tickets for the outdoor screening.
examples.zh: 趁大家都还没花钱买露天放映的票，我先发了一个「暂定安排」。

collocations: make a tentative plan
a tentative plan for Sunday
share a tentative plan with friends

words.enDefinition: To keep the whole afternoon free for a planned activity.

examples.en: I told my roommate to block out the afternoon because the picnic might run long.
examples.zh: 我让室友「腾出整个下午」，因为野餐可能比预想久。

examples.en: Could you block out the afternoon for our group walk if the weather stays clear?
examples.zh: 如果天气一直晴朗，你能「腾出整个下午」跟我们一起散步吗？

collocations: block out the afternoon on your calendar
ask people to block out the afternoon
block out the afternoon for a picnic

words.enDefinition: An informal reply saying you may attend but cannot commit yet.
acceptedEnVariants: put me down as a maybe

examples.en: Please count me as a maybe until I get my shift schedule for next weekend.
examples.zh: 下周末的排班出来前，请「先把我算作待定」。

examples.en: For the picnic, count me as a maybe until my cousin confirms her travel plans.
examples.zh: 野餐「先把我算作待定」吧，我表亲还没确认她什么时候来。

collocations: count me as a maybe for now
count me as a maybe for Sunday
count me as a maybe until tomorrow

words.expression: let's make it a group thing
words.lemma: let's make it a group thing
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to do a proposed activity with more people.
acceptedEnVariants: let's make it a group thing

examples.en: My roommate said “Let's make it a group thing” and suggested inviting our whole floor.
examples.zh: 室友说「咱们约大家一起吧」，提议把我们这层楼的人都约上。

examples.en: Before we buy tickets, let's make it a group thing and ask our seminar friends.
examples.zh: 买票前「咱们约大家一起吧」，先问问研讨课的同学。

collocations: say let's make it a group thing
suggest that we make it a group thing
make it a group thing this time

words.enDefinition: An informal reply saying you want to take part in a suggested activity.

examples.en: I replied “I'm up for it” as soon as they suggested a walk by the river.
examples.zh: 他们一提议去河边散步，我就回了句「我愿意参加」。

examples.en: Maya wrote “I'm up for it” under my message about meeting for coffee on Sunday.
examples.zh: 玛雅在我约大家星期天喝咖啡的消息下说「我愿意参加」。

collocations: say I'm up for it
reply I'm up for it
a message reading I'm up for it

words.enDefinition: A firm reply accepting an invitation when people are counting possible attendees.

examples.en: I'm a definite yes for Friday now that someone has agreed to cover my shift.
examples.zh: 已经有人答应帮我代班了，星期五的活动「我确定参加」。

examples.en: Tell Maya I'm a definite yes before she books the seats for the outdoor film.
examples.zh: 玛雅订露天电影的座位之前，告诉她「我确定参加」。

collocations: I'm a definite yes for Friday
reply I'm a definite yes
tell the group I'm a definite yes

words.enDefinition: A reply saying that you have another arrangement for that time.

examples.en: I already have plans for Saturday, but I can join the picnic on Sunday.
examples.zh: 星期六「我已经有安排了」，但星期天可以参加野餐。

examples.en: I said “I already have plans” when they asked me to come out after class.
examples.zh: 他们问我下课后要不要一起出去，我说「我已经有安排了」。

collocations: say I already have plans
reply I already have plans
I already have plans for that evening

words.enDefinition: A friendly way to decline or qualify an invitation by giving a reason.

examples.en: I'd love to, but I promised to help my roommate move her desk this evening.
examples.zh: 「我很想去，不过」我答应了今晚帮室友搬书桌。

examples.en: I'd love to, but my shift ends too late for me to catch the film.
examples.zh: 「我很想去，不过」我下班太晚，赶不上电影。

collocations: reply I'd love to, but
I'd love to, but I have class
I'd love to, but I'm working

words.enDefinition: To choose not to take part in this particular shared activity.

examples.en: I think I'll sit this one out because I have an early class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天有早课，想「这次先不参加」。

examples.en: Mina said she'd sit this one out and join us for the picnic next week.
examples.zh: 米娜说她「这次先不参加」，下周再来和我们一起野餐。

collocations: decide to sit this one out
have to sit this one out
sit this one out for now

words.expression: leave me out of the booking
words.lemma: leave me out of the booking
words.enDefinition: A request not to include the speaker when reserving seats or tickets for the group.
acceptedEnVariants: leave me out of the booking

examples.en: Please leave me out of the booking if you have to pay for everyone today.
examples.zh: 如果今天必须一次性付齐，「预订时别算我」。

examples.en: You can leave me out of the booking because my ticket is already covered.
examples.zh: 我的票已经有了，「预订时别算我」。

collocations: ask them to leave me out of the booking
leave me out of the booking for now
please leave me out of the booking

words.expression: I can come for a bit
words.lemma: i can come for a bit
words.enDefinition: A reply saying you can join an event for only part of it.
acceptedEnVariants: I can come for a bit

examples.en: I can come for a bit before heading back to campus for my evening class.
examples.zh: 晚课前我得回学校，不过「我能来待一小会儿」。

examples.en: Tell Mina I can come for a bit if the picnic starts before my shift.
examples.zh: 告诉米娜，如果野餐在我上班前开始，「我能来待一小会儿」。

collocations: I can come for a bit after work
say I can come for a bit
reply I can come for a bit

words.enDefinition: A question asking if it is okay to arrive or take part after others begin.

examples.en: Can I join later if my class finishes after you've already ordered your coffees?
examples.zh: 如果你们点完咖啡我才下课，「我晚点能加入吗」？

examples.en: Can I join later once I've dropped my bag off at the residence hall?
examples.zh: 我先把包放回宿舍，「晚点能加入吗」？

collocations: ask can I join later
can I join later after class
can I join later this evening

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time up to which someone can remain at an event.

examples.en: I can stay until eight, when I need to catch my last bus home.
examples.zh: 「我可以待到八点」，之后得去赶回家的末班公交车。

examples.en: I can stay until the film ends if we start before seven this evening.
examples.zh: 如果今晚七点前开始，「我可以待到电影结束」。

collocations: I can stay until eight
say I can stay until
I can stay until the end

words.expression: when do you need an answer
words.lemma: when do you need an answer
words.zhGloss: 你最晚什么时候要答复
words.enDefinition: Asks by what time you need to decide whether to accept an invitation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你最晚什么时候要答复
acceptedEnVariants: when do you need an answer

examples.en: When do you need an answer about Saturday if I might be working that morning?
examples.zh: 我星期六上午可能要上班，关于那天的安排「你最晚什么时候要答复」？

examples.en: When do you need an answer about the craft workshop, before you book or later?
examples.zh: 手工活动「你最晚什么时候要答复」，是订位置之前，还是之后也行？

collocations: ask when do you need an answer
when do you need an answer about Saturday
ask the group when do you need an answer

words.enDefinition: A question suggesting Saturday as an alternative to a previously proposed time.

examples.en: I'm working on Friday, so would Saturday work instead for our picnic by the river?
examples.zh: 我星期五要上班，所以河边野餐「改到星期六行吗」？

examples.en: Would Saturday work instead if everyone is busy with the exhibition setup on Friday?
examples.zh: 如果大家星期五都忙着布展，「改到星期六行吗」？

collocations: ask would Saturday work instead
would Saturday work instead for the picnic
say would Saturday work instead

words.enDefinition: A question asking to move a shared activity to a different day.

examples.en: Could we do another day for coffee if your class ends too late this evening?
examples.zh: 如果你今晚下课太晚，喝咖啡「能改天吗」？

examples.en: Could we do another day when more people are free to see the film?
examples.zh: 「能改天吗」？找个有更多人有空看电影的日子。

collocations: ask could we do another day
could we do another day for coffee
could we do another day this week

words.enDefinition: A suggestion to aim to do the activity sometime in the following week.

examples.en: Let's try for next week because both of us have coursework due on Friday.
examples.zh: 咱俩星期五都要交作业，「咱们试试约在下周吧」。

examples.en: Let's try for next week, when the common room should have more free seats.
examples.zh: 「咱们试试约在下周吧」，到时候公共休息室应该有更多空位。

collocations: suggest let's try for next week
say let's try for next week
let's try for next week instead

words.enDefinition: A conversational phrase used to suggest a particular time or place for a plan.

examples.en: Shall we say six so everyone has time to get there after the afternoon class?
examples.zh: 「要不定在六点」，这样大家下午下课后都来得及赶到？

examples.en: Shall we say the main entrance because there are three doors facing the courtyard?
examples.zh: 朝庭院的门有三扇，「要不定在正门」？

collocations: shall we say six
ask shall we say half past
shall we say the main entrance

words.enDefinition: Introduces a time by which the speaker can get to the meeting place.

examples.en: I can be there by seven if I take the bus right after class.
examples.zh: 如果下课后马上坐公交，「我最晚七点能到」。

examples.en: I can be there by the start of the film even if I miss the first bus.
examples.zh: 即使错过第一趟公交，「我最晚也能在电影开场时到」。

collocations: I can be there by seven
tell the group I can be there by
I can be there by the break

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time a class ends when explaining when you can meet.

examples.en: I've got class until six, so can we get coffee a little later today?
examples.zh: 「我的课要上到六点」，今天能晚一点再喝咖啡吗？

examples.en: I've got class until lunchtime, but I can meet you after your library shift.
examples.zh: 「我的课要上到午饭时间」，但你在图书馆下班后我可以见你。

collocations: I've got class until six
say I've got class until
I've got class until lunchtime

words.enDefinition: A reply saying the speaker can adjust to the time other people choose.

examples.en: I'm flexible on the time because my only Saturday class was canceled this week.
examples.zh: 我星期六唯一一节课这周取消了，「时间我可以配合」。

examples.en: I'm flexible on the time if you want to wait for Mina's shift to end.
examples.zh: 如果你们想等米娜下班，「时间我可以配合」。

collocations: say I'm flexible on the time
tell the group I'm flexible on the time
I'm flexible on the time this weekend

words.enDefinition: A phrase offering any time once the relevant class has finished.

examples.en: I can meet any time after class, so choose a time that suits the others.
examples.zh: 「下课后什么时候都行」，你选个其他人方便的时间吧。

examples.en: My roommate said we could start any time after class, since her shift was canceled.
examples.zh: 室友说她不用上班了，我们「下课后什么时候开始都行」。

collocations: be free any time after class
meet any time after class
come by any time after class

words.enDefinition: A question asking what the group is planning to do that evening.

examples.en: What's the plan for tonight now that the film we wanted to see has sold out?
examples.zh: 想看的电影已经没票了，「今晚怎么安排」？

examples.en: What's the plan for tonight if our usual common room is booked until eight?
examples.zh: 如果常去的公共休息室被预订到八点，「今晚怎么安排」？

collocations: ask what's the plan for tonight
what's the plan for tonight after class
say what's the plan for tonight

words.enDefinition: Asks whether an activity scheduled for a time or day is still happening.

examples.en: Are we still on for Friday even though our afternoon lecture has been moved online?
examples.zh: 虽然星期五下午的讲座改成线上了，「那天的安排还照旧吗」？

examples.en: Are we still on for coffee after class now that your shift starts earlier?
examples.zh: 你上班时间提前了，「下课后还照原计划去喝咖啡吗」？

collocations: are we still on for Friday
are we still on for coffee
ask are we still on for Saturday

words.expression: let's stick with the original plan
words.lemma: let's stick with the original plan
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to keep a plan instead of changing to a newly discussed option.
acceptedEnVariants: let's stick with the original plan

examples.en: Let's stick with the original plan since four people have already bought their tickets.
examples.zh: 已经有四个人买票了，「咱们还是按原计划吧」。

examples.en: Let's stick with the original plan while the weather is still looking good for Sunday.
examples.zh: 看起来星期天天气还不错，「咱们还是按原计划吧」。

collocations: say let's stick with the original plan
let's stick with the original plan for now
reply let's stick with the original plan

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time or place that someone remembers agreeing to earlier.

examples.en: I thought we said six, but the message from Mina said half past five.
examples.zh: 「我以为咱们说好的是六点」，但米娜的消息写的是五点半。

examples.en: I thought we said the main gate rather than the entrance beside the sports hall.
examples.zh: 「我以为咱们说好的是正门」，不是体育馆旁的入口。

collocations: I thought we said six
I thought we said Friday
I thought we said the main gate

words.enDefinition: To choose a definite time so the arrangement can go ahead.

examples.en: We need to lock in a time before Mina buys all the tickets tonight.
examples.zh: 米娜今晚买齐所有票之前，我们得「把时间敲定」。

examples.en: Could we lock in a time for coffee after everyone checks their class schedule?
examples.zh: 等大家检查完课表，能不能「敲定时间」一起喝咖啡？

collocations: lock in a time for Saturday
lock in a time that works
need to lock in a time

words.enDefinition: To wait and decide what to do as the situation becomes clearer.

examples.en: Let's play it by ear because we won't know whether the courtyard is free until noon.
examples.zh: 我们要到中午才知道庭院能不能用，所以「看情况再定」吧。

examples.en: We can play it by ear until we find out when the exhibition closes.
examples.zh: 先「看情况再定」吧，得等确定展览几点关门。

collocations: play it by ear tomorrow
decide to play it by ear
play it by ear if it rains

words.enDefinition: To avoid agreeing on a specific time until more information is available.

examples.en: We decided to leave the time open until Maya had checked her weekend shifts.
examples.zh: 我们决定「先不定具体时间」，等玛雅查完周末排班再说。

examples.en: Can we leave the time open until everyone has checked their shifts for that weekend?
examples.zh: 能不能「先不定具体时间」，等大家看完那个周末的排班？

collocations: leave the time open for now
decide to leave the time open
leave the time open until Friday

words.expression: pick a day that suits everyone
words.lemma: pick a day that suits everyone
words.zhGloss: 选个大家都方便的日子
words.enDefinition: To choose a date when all members of the group can attend.
acceptedZhAnswers: 选个大家都方便的日子
acceptedEnVariants: pick a day that suits everyone

examples.en: Let's pick a day that suits everyone before we ask about borrowing the common room.
examples.zh: 打听能不能借用公共休息室之前，先「选个大家都方便的日子」吧。

examples.en: We used the group chat to pick a day that suits everyone for our picnic.
examples.zh: 我们在群聊里为野餐「选了个大家都方便的日子」。

collocations: try to pick a day that suits everyone
pick a day that suits everyone in the group
let's pick a day that suits everyone

words.enDefinition: Having made two commitments for the same time.

examples.en: I realized I was double-booked when my roommate reminded me about our cinema tickets.
examples.zh: 室友提醒我电影票的事，我才发现自己「同时有两个安排」。

examples.en: Maya was double-booked for Sunday afternoon and couldn't stay for the whole picnic after all.
examples.zh: 玛雅星期天下午「同时有两个安排」，所以最后没能全程参加野餐。

collocations: be double-booked on Friday
realize you're double-booked
be double-booked for the evening

words.enDefinition: To decide not to take part in something after previously agreeing to join.

examples.en: I had to back out of the plan when my supervisor changed my Saturday shift.
examples.zh: 主管调整了我星期六的班次，我只得「退出已经约好的活动」。

examples.en: She didn't want to back out of the plan after everyone had already bought tickets.
examples.zh: 大家都已经买了票，她不想再「退出已经约好的活动」。

collocations: have to back out of the plan
decide to back out of the plan
back out of the plan at the last minute

words.enDefinition: A change to what the group previously agreed to do.

examples.en: There was a change of plans after we found out the courtyard would be closed.
examples.zh: 得知庭院会关闭后，「安排有变」。

examples.en: I sent a quick message about a change of plans before anyone left their residence hall.
examples.zh: 大家还没从宿舍楼出发，我赶紧发消息说「安排有变」。

collocations: announce a change of plans
a small change of plans
message everyone about a change of plans

words.enDefinition: To cancel the activity that had been planned for that evening.

examples.en: We may need to call it off for tonight if the common room stays closed.
examples.zh: 如果公共休息室继续关闭，我们可能得「取消今晚的安排」。

examples.en: Let's call it off for tonight and try again when more friends are around.
examples.zh: 「取消今晚的安排」吧，等更多朋友有空再试。

collocations: decide to call it off for tonight
have to call it off for tonight
call it off for tonight and try again

words.enDefinition: A request to let the group start or continue without the speaker taking part.

examples.en: Go ahead without me if my class runs over and you want to order.
examples.zh: 要是我上课拖堂，而你们又想点单了，「你们不用等我」。

examples.en: You can go ahead without me because I don't know when my shift will finish.
examples.zh: 我不知道什么时候下班，「你们不用等我」。

collocations: tell them to go ahead without me
go ahead without me if I'm late
go ahead without me and order

words.enDefinition: A question asking the group to agree on a place to meet.

examples.en: Where should we meet if the area outside the library is too crowded today?
examples.zh: 今天图书馆外面如果太挤，「咱们在哪儿碰头」？

examples.en: Where should we meet before the film if half the group is coming by bus?
examples.zh: 如果有一半人坐公交来，「电影开始前咱们在哪儿碰头」？

collocations: ask where should we meet
where should we meet after class
where should we meet before the film

words.enDefinition: A place where the same people regularly meet.

examples.en: Shall we meet at the usual place before heading to the craft market together?
examples.zh: 咱们要不要先在「老地方」碰头，再一起去手工艺集市？

examples.en: I'll be at the usual place after class with the books I borrowed from you.
examples.zh: 下课后我会带着跟你借的书去「老地方」。

collocations: meet at the usual place
wait in the usual place
go to the usual place after class

words.expression: can you send me the address
words.lemma: can you send me the address
words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to send the address of a meeting place.
acceptedEnVariants: can you send me the address

examples.en: Can you send me the address before I get on the bus to the picnic?
examples.zh: 我坐公交车去野餐之前，「你能把地址发给我吗」？

examples.en: Can you send me the address so I can check which entrance faces the park?
examples.zh: 「你能把地址发给我吗」？我想看看哪个入口朝着公园。

collocations: can you send me the address again
text can you send me the address
ask can you send me the address

words.enDefinition: A plan to meet someone outside the front of a building or venue.

examples.en: I'll meet you out front when the library closes so we can go together.
examples.zh: 图书馆关门后，我会「在正门外和你碰头」，这样咱们可以一起走。

examples.en: We can meet you out front before everyone heads into the student center for the film.
examples.zh: 大家进学生活动中心看电影前，我们可以「在正门外和你碰头」。

collocations: I'll meet you out front
we'll meet you out front
meet you out front after class

words.enDefinition: Asks which entrance a person is waiting at when a venue has several.

examples.en: Which entrance are you at now that they've opened both doors to the hall?
examples.zh: 大厅两扇门都开了，「你在哪个入口」？

examples.en: I texted “Which entrance are you at?” after walking around the sports center twice.
examples.zh: 我绕体育馆走了两圈后，发消息问：“「你在哪个入口」？”

collocations: text “Which entrance are you at?”
ask which entrance someone is at
which entrance are you at right now

words.enDefinition: A message saying you are at an entrance other than the one your group agreed on.

examples.en: I think I'm at the wrong entrance because I can only see the car park.
examples.zh: 我只能看见停车场，可能「我走错入口了」。

examples.en: I texted “I'm at the wrong entrance” after seeing the sign for the staff offices.
examples.zh: 看见员工办公室的指示牌后，我发消息说「我走错入口了」。

collocations: say I'm at the wrong entrance
text I'm at the wrong entrance
tell your friends I'm at the wrong entrance

words.expression: text me when you get here
words.lemma: text me when you get here
words.enDefinition: A request for someone to send a message when they reach the meeting place.
acceptedEnVariants: text me when you get here

examples.en: Text me when you get here and I'll come downstairs to meet you outside.
examples.zh: 「你到了给我发消息」，我就下楼到外面接你。

examples.en: Just text me when you get here because the doorbell in our lounge is broken.
examples.zh: 我们休息室的门铃坏了，「你到了给我发消息」就行。

collocations: say text me when you get here
please text me when you get here
just text me when you get here

words.enDefinition: A message reporting that you arrived at the meeting place a moment ago.

examples.en: I just got here, and the queue outside the cinema is already around the corner.
examples.zh: 「我刚到」，电影院外的队伍已经排到拐角了。

examples.en: I just got here, but I can't see anyone from our class in the lobby.
examples.zh: 「我刚到」，不过在大厅没看见咱们班的人。

collocations: say I just got here
text I just got here
tell them I just got here

words.enDefinition: A question asking how far someone is from where you plan to meet.

examples.en: Kai asked “How far away are you?” when the doors opened five minutes early.
examples.zh: 门提前五分钟开了，凯就问「你离这儿还有多远」？

examples.en: I asked “How far away are you?” so we could decide whether to order yet.
examples.zh: 我问「你离这儿还有多远」，好决定现在要不要点单。

collocations: text how far away are you
ask how far away are you
how far away are you now

words.enDefinition: A message estimating you will reach the meeting place in about ten minutes.

examples.en: I'm about ten minutes away, so you can start picking out a spot on the lawn.
examples.zh: 「我大概还有十分钟到」，你们可以先在草坪上挑个地方。

examples.en: I sent “I'm about ten minutes away” as the bus left the stop outside campus.
examples.zh: 公交车离开校园外的站点时，我发消息说「我大概还有十分钟到」。

collocations: text I'm about ten minutes away
tell the group I'm about ten minutes away
say I'm about ten minutes away

words.enDefinition: An informal invitation allowing someone to arrive at any convenient time.

examples.en: We're staying in the lounge all afternoon, so come whenever you finish your assignment.
examples.zh: 我们整个下午都在休息室，你写完作业「随时来都行」。

examples.en: Mina said we could come whenever, since the picnic didn't have an official start time.
examples.zh: 野餐没有正式的开始时间，米娜说我们「随时来都行」。

collocations: come whenever you're free
come whenever you can
tell someone to come whenever

words.enDefinition: To go to the agreed meeting place with other people rather than separately.

examples.en: We can head over together once you put your notebook back in your room.
examples.zh: 你把笔记本放回房间后，我们可以「一起过去」。

examples.en: I asked if they wanted to head over together after the seminar finished at noon.
examples.zh: 我问他们中午研讨课结束后要不要「一起过去」。

collocations: head over together after class
wait and head over together
head over together from campus

words.enDefinition: A message confirming you will go separately and see the other person at the destination.

examples.en: I'll meet you there after I return these books to the library across the road.
examples.zh: 我把这些书还到马路对面的图书馆后，「在那儿跟你碰头」。

examples.en: I'll meet you there because I need to go back for my jacket before the film.
examples.zh: 电影开始前，我得回去拿夹克，所以「我在那儿跟你碰头」。

collocations: say I'll meet you there
text I'll meet you there
I'll meet you there after class

words.enDefinition: To enter a building or venue at the same time as a group.

examples.en: We agreed to go in together so the usher could see all our tickets at once.
examples.zh: 我们说好「一起进去」，这样引座员能一次看完所有人的票。

examples.en: Do you want to go in together when the rest of our group gets here?
examples.zh: 等我们小组其他人到了，你想「一起进去」吗？

collocations: wait to go in together
decide to go in together
go in together once everyone arrives

words.enDefinition: A casual suggestion to enter a venue now.

examples.en: Shall we head in before the film starts and all the seats fill up?
examples.zh: 「咱们要进去吗」？电影快开场了，座位说不定很快就坐满。

examples.en: Shall we head in now that everyone has found their ticket on their phone?
examples.zh: 大家都在手机上找到各自的票了，「咱们要进去吗」？

collocations: ask shall we head in
shall we head in now
shall we head in before the rain

words.enDefinition: A request for someone to wait outdoors near the agreed place.

examples.en: Can you wait for me outside while I return these books at the library desk?
examples.zh: 我去图书馆柜台还这些书时，你能「在外面等我」吗？

examples.en: Please wait for me outside because I forgot my jacket in the common room.
examples.zh: 我把夹克忘在公共休息室了，请「在外面等我」。

collocations: please wait for me outside
ask you to wait for me outside
can you wait for me outside

words.enDefinition: A request to join the speaker's group at the place they indicate.

examples.en: Come find us by the window when you finish speaking with the tutor upstairs.
examples.zh: 你在楼上跟导师聊完后，「到窗边来找我们」。

examples.en: I told her to come find us once she had picked up her own coffee.
examples.zh: 我叫她拿到自己的咖啡后就「过来找我们」。

collocations: come find us inside
tell them to come find us
come find us by the window

words.enDefinition: Introduces a visible landmark near where the group is waiting.

examples.en: We're over by the steps near the fountain, where there is room for your bike.
examples.zh: 「我们在喷泉附近的台阶旁边」，这里有地方停你的自行车。

examples.en: We're over by the window in the corner so everyone can see us from outside.
examples.zh: 「我们在角落的窗边」，大家从外面也能看到我们。

collocations: we're over by the steps
we're over by the window
text we're over by the entrance

words.enDefinition: A reservation made together for several people attending the same activity.

examples.en: We made a group booking for the screening because everyone wanted to sit together.
examples.zh: 我们做了放映活动的「团体预订」，因为大家想坐在一起。

examples.en: Maya checked the group booking before telling everyone which entrance to use on Saturday.
examples.zh: 玛雅查了「团体预订」信息，才通知大家星期六走哪个入口。

collocations: make a group booking
change a group booking
a group booking for six

words.enDefinition: To reserve seats next to each other so friends can stay together.

examples.en: Can we book seats together for the afternoon film before the middle rows fill up?
examples.zh: 下午的电影能不能赶在中间几排坐满前，「预订相邻的座位」？

examples.en: We tried to book seats together, but only one pair was left near the front.
examples.zh: 我们想「预订相邻的座位」，但只剩前面有两个挨着的位置。

collocations: try to book seats together
book seats together for the screening
ask if we can book seats together

words.enDefinition: A reservation recorded using the speaker’s name.

examples.en: There is a booking under my name for our group at seven this evening.
examples.zh: 今天晚上七点有「用我名字订的位置」，是给我们小组的。

examples.en: I told Kai to ask for the booking under my name when he arrived first.
examples.zh: 凯先到，我让他问一下「用我名字订的位置」。

collocations: a booking under my name
find the booking under my name
check the booking under my name

words.enDefinition: To gather the people taking part in the shared activity.

examples.en: Could you round up the group while I check whether our seats are ready?
examples.zh: 我去看看座位有没有准备好，你能「把大家叫到一起」吗？

examples.en: We need to round up the group for a photo before everyone starts leaving.
examples.zh: 大家陆续离开之前，我们得「把大家叫到一起」拍张照。

collocations: help round up the group
try to round up the group
round up the group for a photo

words.enDefinition: To choose a place to sit, stand, or gather for an activity.

examples.en: Can you pick a spot in the shade while I get the picnic blanket?
examples.zh: 我去拿野餐毯时，你能「在阴凉处挑个位置」吗？

examples.en: Let's pick a spot near the front so the shorter people can see the stage.
examples.zh: 咱们「在靠前的地方挑个位置」吧，让个子矮一点的人也能看到舞台。

collocations: pick a spot near the front
pick a spot in the shade
pick a spot to meet

words.enDefinition: To spread a blanket out so a group can sit on it for a picnic.

examples.en: We went early to lay out a picnic blanket under the trees near campus.
examples.zh: 我们提前去了校园附近的树下，「把野餐毯铺好」。

examples.en: Can you help lay out a picnic blanket while the others bring over the food?
examples.zh: 其他人把食物拿过来时，你能帮忙「把野餐毯铺好」吗？

collocations: help lay out a picnic blanket
lay out a picnic blanket on the lawn
lay out a picnic blanket in the shade

words.enDefinition: To bring food, drinks, or supplies for people to use or enjoy together.
acceptedEnVariants: bring something for everyone to share

examples.en: Everyone said they could bring something to share when we planned lunch on the lawn.
examples.zh: 计划在草坪吃午饭时，大家都说可以「带点东西来分给大家」。

examples.en: I offered to bring something to share because Mina was already carrying the picnic blanket.
examples.zh: 米娜已经带着野餐毯了，我就主动提出「带点东西来分给大家」。

collocations: ask people to bring something to share
bring something to share with the group
bring something to share at the picnic

words.enDefinition: A question asking what different people plan to bring to a shared activity.

examples.en: What's everyone bringing for the picnic, and do we have enough plates to share?
examples.zh: 野餐「大家都打算带什么」？我们的盘子够不够大家用？

examples.en: What's everyone bringing to the board game afternoon apart from a game to share?
examples.zh: 除了带一款桌游跟大家一起玩，下午的桌游活动「大家都打算带什么」？

collocations: ask what's everyone bringing
what's everyone bringing for lunch
check by asking what's everyone bringing

words.enDefinition: A question asking what items would be useful or expected at a group gathering.

examples.en: What should I bring for the picnic if you already have blankets and drinks?
examples.zh: 如果你们已经有毯子和饮料了，野餐时「我该带什么」？

examples.en: What should I bring besides snacks for the film night in your common room?
examples.zh: 在你们公共休息室看电影，除了零食「我还该带什么」？

collocations: ask what should I bring
what should I bring for the picnic
what should I bring besides snacks

words.enDefinition: A request for each person attending an activity to supply snacks for themselves.

examples.en: The note said “Bring your own snacks” because the screening room did not sell food.
examples.zh: 放映室不卖吃的，通知上写着「自带零食」。

examples.en: Mina wrote “Bring your own snacks” at the top of the group chat message.
examples.zh: 米娜在群聊消息的开头写了「自带零食」。

collocations: a sign saying bring your own snacks
a note reading bring your own snacks
bring your own snacks to the screening

words.enDefinition: A message telling others that food is already taken care of for the gathering.

examples.en: We've got the food covered, so could you bring the blanket from your room?
examples.zh: 「吃的我们来安排」，你能从房间带条毯子来吗？

examples.en: Tell Maya we've got the food covered because two classmates are making sandwiches this morning.
examples.zh: 告诉玛雅「吃的我们来安排」，今天上午有两位同学做三明治。

collocations: say we've got the food covered
tell everyone we've got the food covered
we've got the food covered for Saturday

words.enDefinition: To contribute part of the money for something a group is buying.

examples.en: We decided to chip in for pizza after the film ran longer than expected.
examples.zh: 电影比预想的长，我们决定「一起出钱买」比萨。

examples.en: Would everyone chip in for a larger bag of popcorn to share during the film?
examples.zh: 大家愿不愿意「一起出钱买」一大袋爆米花，看电影时一起吃？

collocations: chip in for pizza
chip in for the room
ask everyone to chip in for snacks

words.enDefinition: To share a cost equally with one other person.

examples.en: My roommate offered to go halves on the picnic supplies because we were shopping together.
examples.zh: 我和室友一起采购，她提出野餐用品「各付一半」。

examples.en: Could we go halves on the larger bag of popcorn if you're sharing it too?
examples.zh: 你也吃的话，我们能「各付一半买」大袋爆米花吗？

collocations: go halves on a bag of snacks
offer to go halves on something
go halves on the picnic supplies

words.expression: how much do I owe you
words.lemma: how much do i owe you
words.enDefinition: A question asking how much to pay back to someone who covered a shared expense.
acceptedEnVariants: how much do I owe you

examples.en: How much do I owe you for the two tickets you bought for us yesterday?
examples.zh: 昨天你帮我们买了两张票，「我该给你多少钱」？

examples.en: How much do I owe you for my share of the picnic supplies today?
examples.zh: 今天野餐用品我该出的那一份，「我该给你多少钱」？

collocations: ask how much do I owe you
how much do I owe you for the tickets
text how much do I owe you

words.enDefinition: An invitation phrase saying it is fine to decline or skip the event.

examples.en: No pressure to come if you need the evening to finish your assignment.
examples.zh: 如果你晚上得留时间写完作业，「来不来都没关系」。

examples.en: I added “No pressure to come” because I knew my roommate had an exam tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我知道室友明天有考试，就加了一句「来不来都没关系」。

collocations: tell them there's no pressure to come
a message saying no pressure to come
say no pressure to come

words.enDefinition: A condition meaning that the weather needs to remain suitable for a planned activity.

examples.en: We'll eat on the lawn if the weather holds until the end of class.
examples.zh: 「如果天气一直不错」到下课，我们就去草坪上吃。

examples.en: If the weather holds, we can leave our coats at home for the walk.
examples.zh: 「如果天气一直不错」，咱们散步时就可以把外套留在家里。

collocations: meet outside if the weather holds
go ahead if the weather holds
eat on the lawn if the weather holds

words.enDefinition: To change the location of a planned activity from outside to inside.

examples.en: We can move it indoors if the tables outside are still wet after lunch.
examples.zh: 如果午饭后室外桌子还是湿的，我们可以「把活动移到室内」。

examples.en: Mina suggested we move it indoors because the wind kept knocking over the cups.
examples.zh: 风老是把杯子刮倒，米娜建议我们「把活动移到室内」。

collocations: decide to move it indoors
ask whether to move it indoors
move it indoors if it rains

words.expression: come and go as you please
words.lemma: come and go as you please
words.enDefinition: To arrive and leave at any time you choose during an informal event.
acceptedEnVariants: come and go as you please
come and go as you like

examples.en: You can come and go as you please while we share snacks in the lounge.
examples.zh: 我们在休息室一起吃零食时，大家「随时来去都可以」。

examples.en: The notice said “Come and go as you please” below the picnic start time.
examples.zh: 告示在野餐开始时间下方写着「随时来去都可以」。

collocations: feel free to come and go as you please
a message saying come and go as you please
tell friends to come and go as they please

words.enDefinition: To turn a planned activity into a longer evening out or celebration.

examples.en: Let's make an evening of it and get dinner together before the outdoor film.
examples.zh: 「咱们安排一整晚的活动」吧，先吃饭再去看露天电影。

examples.en: We decided to make an evening of it after handing in our last assignment.
examples.zh: 交完最后一份作业后，我们决定「安排一整晚的活动」庆祝一下。

collocations: decide to make an evening of it
suggest we make an evening of it
make an evening of it after exams

words.enDefinition: To choose a film by asking the group to vote for its preference.

examples.en: Can we vote on a film before I go to buy anything for the evening?
examples.zh: 我去买晚上用的东西前，咱们能先「投票选一部电影」吗？

examples.en: We decided to vote on a film because nobody had agreed on a comedy yet.
examples.zh: 大家还没选定要看的喜剧，我们决定「投票选一部电影」。

collocations: ask everyone to vote on a film
vote on a film in the chat
vote on a film for Friday

words.enDefinition: To alternate who gets to choose something for a group.
acceptedEnVariants: take it in turns to pick

examples.en: We take turns picking films so everyone gets to show the group something they like.
examples.zh: 我们「轮流挑选」电影，让每个人都能放一部自己喜欢的片子给大家看。

examples.en: Could we take turns picking the music while we wait for the others to arrive?
examples.zh: 等其他人过来的时候，咱们能「轮流挑选」音乐吗？

collocations: take turns picking films
take turns picking songs
agree to take turns picking

words.enDefinition: A list of songs that several people can listen to or add to.

examples.en: We made a shared playlist so each friend could suggest songs for the picnic.
examples.zh: 我们做了个「共享播放列表」，让每位朋友都能为野餐推荐歌曲。

examples.en: Kai put on the shared playlist while we waited for everyone to finish their coffee.
examples.zh: 我们等大家喝完咖啡时，凯播放了「共享播放列表」。

collocations: make a shared playlist
add a song to a shared playlist
put on a shared playlist

words.enDefinition: To delay starting an activity until the rest of the group arrives.

examples.en: Let's wait for the others before starting the game because we're still missing two players.
examples.zh: 还有两位玩家没到，咱们「等其他人到了再开始」玩吧。

examples.en: We chose to wait for the others before ordering drinks at the cafe near campus.
examples.zh: 在校园附近的咖啡馆，我们决定「等其他人都到了再点饮料」。

collocations: decide to wait for the others
ask if we should wait for the others
wait for the others before starting

words.enDefinition: To move sideways a short distance, usually to make room for someone.

examples.en: Can you scoot over a little so Mina can sit with us on this bench?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边挪一下」吗？这样米娜也能坐到这条长椅上。

examples.en: I asked my roommate to scoot over when our friends arrived with their coffee.
examples.zh: 朋友们拿着咖啡到了，我请室友「往旁边挪一下」。

collocations: ask someone to scoot over
scoot over a little
scoot over on the bench

words.enDefinition: A casual way to ask whether the group can move to another spot nearby.

examples.en: Mind if we move over to the window where we can hear each other better?
examples.zh: 「介意咱们挪到窗边吗」？那里大家更能听清彼此说话。

examples.en: Mind if we move over a little so the other group can use this bench?
examples.zh: 「介意咱们稍微挪个地方吗」？好让另一组人也能用这条长椅。

collocations: ask mind if we move over
mind if we move over to the window
say mind if we move over

words.zhGloss: 帮我们留着排队的位置
words.enDefinition: To keep the group's place in a queue while some people step away briefly.
acceptedZhAnswers: 帮我们留着排队的位置
acceptedEnVariants: hold our place in the queue

examples.en: Could you hold our place in line while we check which screening is starting first?
examples.zh: 我们去看看哪场放映先开始，你能「帮我们留着排队的位置」吗？

examples.en: Maya offered to hold our place in line while we moved our bikes off the path.
examples.zh: 我们去把自行车从通道上挪走时，玛雅主动「帮我们留着排队的位置」。

collocations: ask someone to hold our place in line
hold our place in line for a minute
offer to hold our place in line

words.enDefinition: To leave a room briefly to get fresh air outside.

examples.en: Do you want to step outside for some air before we start the next film?
examples.zh: 开始放下一部电影前，你想「出去透透气」吗？

examples.en: I said I would step outside for some air while everyone chose another game.
examples.zh: 大家在选下一轮玩什么时，我说要「出去透透气」。

collocations: want to step outside for some air
let's step outside for some air
offer to step outside for some air

words.enDefinition: Asks someone to meet or locate the speaker once a performance finishes.

examples.en: Find me after the show and we can get coffee near the bus stop.
examples.zh: 「演出结束后来找我」，咱们可以去公交站附近喝咖啡。

examples.en: I wrote “Find me after the show” on the note I left with Maya.
examples.zh: 我给玛雅留的纸条上写着「演出结束后来找我」。

collocations: tell them to find me after the show
please find me after the show
say find me after the show

words.enDefinition: To get a quick, light bite after a planned activity.

examples.en: Do you want to grab a snack afterward if the film finishes before nine?
examples.zh: 如果电影九点前结束，你想「之后去吃点东西」吗？

examples.en: We decided to grab a snack afterward at the shop next to our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们决定「之后去宿舍楼旁的店里吃点东西」。

collocations: want to grab a snack afterward
suggest we grab a snack afterward
grab a snack afterward near campus

words.enDefinition: To remain a little longer to take part in another round of a game.

examples.en: Can you stay for one more round before you have to catch the bus?
examples.zh: 你去赶公交之前能「留下来再玩一轮」吗？

examples.en: We agreed to stay for one more round because Kai had only just joined us.
examples.zh: 凯刚加入，我们说好「留下来再玩一轮」。

collocations: want to stay for one more round
ask people to stay for one more round
decide to stay for one more round

words.enDefinition: To return on foot to campus or another place with the rest of the group.

examples.en: We can walk back together once the film ends and the lights come up.
examples.zh: 电影结束、灯亮起来后，我们可以「一起走回去」。

examples.en: My roommate asked if we could walk back together after the picnic in the park.
examples.zh: 室友问，公园的野餐结束后我们能不能「一起走回去」。

collocations: offer to walk back together
walk back together after the film
ask if we can walk back together

words.enDefinition: To travel back in the same car with another person or group.

examples.en: Can we share a ride back to campus after the film ends this evening?
examples.zh: 今晚电影结束后，我们能「一起搭车回校园」吗？

examples.en: We decided to share a ride back after finding out the last bus had left.
examples.zh: 得知末班公交已经开走了，我们决定「一起搭车回去」。

collocations: decide to share a ride back
ask if we can share a ride back
share a ride back to campus

words.enDefinition: A suggestion or confirmation to meet again at the same time the following week.

examples.en: Same time next week, or will some of you be preparing for the exhibition?
examples.zh: 「下周同一时间」见，还是你们有人要为展览做准备？

examples.en: We agreed on the same time next week before anyone packed up their board games.
examples.zh: 大家收起桌游之前，我们约好了「下周同一时间」见。

collocations: meet at the same time next week
ask same time next week
plan for the same time next week

words.enDefinition: A picture taken of several people together at the same time.

examples.en: We took a group photo on the steps before everyone left for the bus.
examples.zh: 大家离开去坐公交前，我们在台阶上拍了张「合照」。

examples.en: Mina asked for a group photo while there was still enough light in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 庭院里的光线还够，米娜提议拍张「合照」。

collocations: take a group photo
pose for a group photo
share a group photo

words.expression: are you okay with me posting this
words.lemma: are you okay with me posting this
words.zhGloss: 你介意我把这个发出去吗
words.enDefinition: Asks permission to share something online, such as a photo of the group.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你介意我把这个发出去吗
acceptedEnVariants: are you okay with me posting this

examples.en: Are you okay with me posting this photo from our picnic on my page?
examples.zh: 「你介意我把这张野餐照片发到我主页上吗」？

examples.en: Are you okay with me posting this video from the game in our class chat?
examples.zh: 「你介意我把这段游戏视频发到班级群里吗」？

collocations: ask are you okay with me posting this
text are you okay with me posting this
say are you okay with me posting this

words.enDefinition: To choose the option preferred by most people in the group.

examples.en: We said we'd go with the majority when choosing between the two films tonight.
examples.zh: 我们说好，今晚两部片子只能选一部时就「按多数人的选择来」。

examples.en: Let's go with the majority because everyone has had a chance to choose.
examples.zh: 大家都有机会选过了，「咱们就按多数人的选择来」吧。

collocations: decide to go with the majority
agree to go with the majority
go with the majority if the votes differ

words.enDefinition: Asks whether people in another part of the space can hear clearly.

examples.en: Can everyone hear from there, or should we bring the speaker a little closer?
examples.zh: 「大家在那里听得清吗」？要不要把音箱再拿近一点？

examples.en: I asked “Can everyone hear from there?” before starting the film in our lounge.
examples.zh: 在休息室放电影前，我问了句「大家在那里听得清吗」？

collocations: ask can everyone hear from there
check by saying can everyone hear from there
can everyone hear from there before we start

words.enDefinition: To speak more quietly as a group so others are not disturbed.

examples.en: Let's keep our voices down because the students next door are studying for exams.
examples.zh: 隔壁同学在复习备考，「咱们说话小声点」吧。

examples.en: We tried to keep our voices down while choosing a film in the shared lounge.
examples.zh: 在共用休息室选电影时，我们尽量「说话小声点」。

collocations: try to keep our voices down
need to keep our voices down
ask everyone to keep their voices down

words.enDefinition: To remove used cups so a space is tidy again after a gathering.

examples.en: Could you clear away the cups while I fold the blanket after our picnic?
examples.zh: 野餐完我来叠毯子，你能「把杯子收走」吗？

examples.en: Mina offered to clear away the cups while we returned the chairs to the lounge.
examples.zh: 我们把椅子放回休息室时，米娜主动提出「把杯子收走」。

collocations: help clear away the cups
offer to clear away the cups
clear away the cups from the table

words.expression: leave the place as we found it
words.lemma: leave the place as we found it
words.enDefinition: To restore a shared place to the condition it was in before the group used it.
acceptedEnVariants: leave the place as we found it

examples.en: Let's leave the place as we found it by putting all the tables back afterward.
examples.zh: 「咱们把场地恢复原样」吧，结束后把桌子都放回原位。

examples.en: We wanted to leave the place as we found it after borrowing the common room.
examples.zh: 借用公共休息室之后，我们想「把场地恢复原样」。

collocations: make sure we leave the place as we found it
aim to leave the place as we found it
ask everyone to leave the place as we found it

words.zhGloss: 我能把其他人也约上吗
words.enDefinition: Asks permission to invite additional people to an existing plan.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我能把其他人也约上吗

examples.en: Can I invite the others from our seminar if there's room on the lawn?
examples.zh: 如果草坪上还有地方，「我能把研讨课的其他人也约上吗」？

examples.en: Can I invite the others before I tell Maya how many people are coming?
examples.zh: 在告诉玛雅有多少人来之前，「我能把其他人也约上吗」？

collocations: ask can I invite the others
can I invite the others from class
can I invite the others next time

words.enDefinition: A promise to bring one more of something for a group activity.

examples.en: I'll bring an extra blanket because the bench might be wet at the park.
examples.zh: 公园的长椅可能是湿的，「我会多带一条毯子」。

examples.en: I'll bring an extra chair if your roommate decides to join us for the screening.
examples.zh: 如果你室友决定来一起看电影，「我会多带一把椅子」。

collocations: I'll bring an extra blanket
I'll bring an extra chair
tell the group I'll bring an extra

words.enDefinition: Expresses a wish that the person can attend a planned gathering.

examples.en: Hope you can make it to our picnic once your afternoon class is over.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，「希望你能来」参加我们的野餐。

examples.en: I added “Hope you can make it” when I sent my roommate the updated plan.
examples.zh: 把更新后的安排发给室友时，我加了句「希望你能来」。

collocations: add hope you can make it
say hope you can make it
write hope you can make it
